_comment: SHARED CROSS-TIER FIXTURE. Read by BOTH implementations of the region winding check:
The sign of the signed area depends on the handedness of the lat/long to XYZ mapping.
If the two tiers ever disagree, every verdict inverts: valid regions get 422'd and
clockwise ones sail through. Keeping the cases in ONE file means neither side can
quietly drift its own copy of the expectations.
Points are [latitude, longitude] in traversal order. 'expect' is the classification
The authority for 'counterclockwise' is the orientation EarClipping accepts -- for
regions small enough that EarClipping is trustworthy. It is NOT trustworthy for very
large ones: its #pointInCone assumes all points are coplanar, which a region spanning
a large fraction of the globe badly violates, and it accepts BOTH orientations there.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: rings lying on a great circle with widely-spaced vertices. Three
points 120 degrees apart on the equator give 2*pi (a hemisphere), while 36 points 10
degrees apart give 0 -- the Van Oosterom-Strackee denominator goes negative once the
vertices are far enough apart, flipping the atan2 branch. Both answers are defensible
because a great circle does not say which half you meant, but a sampling-dependent
answer is not a contract. Closely-spaced collinear points ARE stable and are covered.

cases.name: counterclockwise quad
cases.note: The oracle fixture from tests/region-winding.spec.ts. EarClipping triangulates it.

cases.name: clockwise quad
cases.note: The same ring reversed. EarClipping finds no ear and throws.

cases.name: large region spanning 240 degrees of longitude
cases.note: Traced by SHORTEST great-circle arcs, these four points enclose the complementary 120-degree region wound clockwise -- so 'clockwise' is geometrically correct, not a defect. Kept because it pins the one case where the check and EarClipping disagree: EarClipping triangulates this (and its reverse), so a direct API POST of it gets a 422 while the frontend would have drawn it. Benign in the normal flow -- frontend normalization reverses it before submit and EarClipping renders the reversed ring too. NOTE: regionWindingSign also calls this clockwise. The newer check is not an improvement here; see regionSignedArea's header for what it actually buys.

cases.name: collinear meridian
cases.note: Encloses no area, so it has no orientation. Must be 'degenerate', not 'clockwise' - calling it wound the wrong way would be misleading.

cases.name: self-intersecting twist
cases.note: KNOWN GAP, pinned deliberately. Globally counterclockwise but crosses itself, so EarClipping throws while both implementations accept it. Orientation is not simplicity. Contained by the ErrorBoundary around the region mesh; closing it entirely would mean porting EarClipping to the backend.
